title: Pax Silica assessment — change log
policy: Nothing is silently revised. Substantive changes to the site or the assessment are recorded here, newest first. An entry of type correction or removal must quote the superseded text verbatim in 'supersedes', so the maintenance disclosure's claim can be checked against the record rather than taken on trust. Automated daily data refreshes (the news rail, the listening exhibit) are recorded in the repository history, not here, unless they move a finding.

types.addition: new content or evidence published; no prior text displaced
types.update: existing content moved forward by new information; the prior text was not wrong when written
types.correction: previously published text was wrong and is corrected; the superseded text is quoted verbatim
types.removal: previously published text is withdrawn; the withdrawn text is quoted verbatim
types.process: a change to how the site or the assessment is maintained, not to findings

history_before_this_log: Changes before 7 August 2026 are recorded in Appendix H of the assessment (change logs v2.1 through v2.14, in the full report and the PDF) and in the public repository history.

entries.title: A Pampanga Catholic school’s 25 July 2026 call for transparency and a conditional moratorium is added, seven weeks late, as a correction of a coverage omission
entries.summary: The Philippine Daily Inquirer reported on 27 July 2026 that St Scholastica’s Academy in the City of San Fernando, Pampanga — a Catholic Benedictine school run by Missionary Benedictine Sisters — issued a statement on Saturday 25 July which, while recognising the project’s potential to spur economic growth, sought greater transparency and a temporary halt, appealing for a moratorium on implementation until environmental, social and governance concerns are adequately addressed, and for independent scientific assessments of projected water and energy consumption. Its stated ground was that no publicly available comprehensive Environmental Impact Assessment, no complete disclosure of long-term water and energy requirements and no full accounting of effects on host communities and neighbouring provinces including Pampanga had been published. This report did not carry it. The item reached the monitor on 16 September only through an aggregator’s republication, and its body was unreadable that day; it was retrieved in full on 17 September through the browser lane, gated, and applied. It is recorded as a correction of a coverage omission, not as a new development. The timeline, the environmental and social section and the stakeholder analysis record it with the limits of its sourcing: no primary copy of the statement and no independent carrier was located, so its date, contents and quotations rest on one Tier-3 report, and 25 July is the article’s “On Saturday” read against a Monday publication. It is a school’s institutional statement, not a diocesan or bishops’-conference position, and it is not counted in the opposition coalition. Pampanga is a neighbouring, not the host, province, and no claim is made that this was the first institutional position from Pampanga. One adversarial finding-level gate pass returned UNREFUTED-WITH-CAVEATS with ten caveats, every one honoured; asked directly, it held that nothing here justifies moving a Key Judgment, confidence level, scenario weight, precondition, red line or claim-checker verdict, and the plotted stakeholder coordinates do not move. One source is registered (T3-90). The “project facts verified to” date advances to 17 September 2026.

entries.title: A reported description of the November instrument as a BCDA master agreement with an unnamed US counterpart is added, and passages describing the signing as the two governments’ own, and the site as settled “state land”, are corrected
entries.summary: Six reports of 14–15 September, carriers of the same press encounter rather than independent confirmation, attribute to Trade Undersecretary Ceferino Rodolfo a description of the contemplated November instrument as a master agreement between BCDA and an unnamed US counterpart, which BusinessMirror reports he said would not be signed directly by the Philippine and US governments. The outlets differ on its structure; Manila Bulletin alone reports a lease of the property to a US agency. No text, transcript, official release or US confirmation was located, so its legal form, parties and effects at signature remain unestablished. The timeline, legal section and the November claim note record this. Corrections: the executive summary and FAQ said both governments hope to sign the framework; they now say Philippine officials hope BCDA and an unidentified US counterpart will sign a contemplated framework or master agreement. “State land” is replaced where it could read as a settled classification under RA 7652 and RA 12252, which remains open. The SINAG paragraph records a second, overlapping BusinessWorld report of Jayson Cainglet’s statement and adds former Agriculture Secretary William D. Dar’s conditional position. Two adversarial finding-level gate passes: the first refused three of five amendments and supplied the wording now published; the second cleared all seven and required the executive-summary and FAQ corrections. Eight sources are registered (T3-83 to T3-89, T1-57). No Key Judgment, confidence level, scenario weight, precondition, red line, stakeholder coordinate, implementation-gate count or claim-checker verdict moves. The “project facts verified to” date advances to 15 September 2026.

entries.title: A reported release on bail, two press-conference remarks that Pax Silica details were still under deliberation, an Iloilo City protest and an agriculture group’s conditions are added, each with the limits of its sourcing
entries.summary: Philstar reported on 14 September, attributing its account to Karapatan, that the five people arrested at the 10 September protest each posted ₱60,000 bail on 12 September and were released. No court, judicial approval, bail receipt, release order or official confirmation was located, so this remains an advocacy organisation’s account carried by one outlet, and posting bail establishes neither an offence nor a court filing. The report’s 13 September statements that no second carrier had been found and that no retrieved record established that bail was posted are dated and recorded as superseded rather than silently replaced. Philstar’s roster agrees with TV5’s Karapatan-attributed list, which narrows but does not resolve the roster discrepancy. Daily Tribune reported Finance Undersecretary Angela Ignacio calling Pax Silica “a work in progress” and Ambassador Heather Variava calling it “an agreement that’s under deliberation” at the forum’s 10 September press conference; both quotations are single-carrier, neither identifies the unfinished instrument, and neither moves the November target. An 11 September Iloilo City mobilisation led by the League of Filipino Students–Panay is added; the withdrawn Oton data-centre proposal and the Iloilo governor’s August “Iloilo version” remark are not treated as Pax Silica projects. SINAG executive director Jayson Cainglet’s conditional safeguards are added as BusinessMirror reported them, and SINAG is not counted in the opposition coalition. Two adversarial finding-level gate passes: the first refused three of five amendments, the second cleared all five with no wording change required. Seven sources are registered (T3-76 to T3-82). No Key Judgment, confidence level, scenario weight, precondition, red line, stakeholder coordinate or claim-checker row moves. The “project facts verified to” date advances to 14 September 2026.

entries.title: Seventeen editorial questions left open by the whole-document corrections are decided; eight sources are verified and registered, and three published figures are corrected
entries.summary: The corrections published in v1.95 were held to the review's minimum and left seventeen judgment calls open; each is now decided (report Appendix H.50). KJ-6 keeps High confidence, re-grounded on its narrower judgment that the published tax and employment figures are not reconciled at every effective rate from 10% to 20%. KJ-8's rationale is limited to what the Energy Secretary's statement supports, grid connection, and its undefined "near-site" becomes the site and New Clark City. Risk R3's likelihood moves from Medium-High to Medium: the premise it rested on was withdrawn in v2.52, and a dedicated long-term water supply has entered procurement without an identified source; its impact stays Very high. The withholding-tax claim keeps its misleading status with a corrected label. Summary statements of cost, control and certainty are scoped: most no-regret actions are low-cost but two need funded studies and regulator positions; three sensitivities turn on Philippine decisions rather than executive control; Scenario B is likely, not certain, to be reported as a failure. The LNG study is the only firm-generation option with reported feasibility funding, beside a dedicated plant of unspecified fuel under study. The export's exclusion of reposts is confirmed from the data, the ×10 pre-seam bars are kept as a disclosed scale convention, PNA is filed as Tier 3, and claim 50's metadata points to the source note that carries the roster disclosure. Eight sources are verified and registered (T1-51 to T1-56, T3-74, T3-75). Corrections found in doing so: the USTR Section 301 notice was published in the Federal Register on 28 July 2026, not 23 July; RA 12066 was approved on 8 November 2024, not 11 November; and 4,106 MW on 15 May 2026 was capacity unavailable to the grid, not all on forced outage. The two 13 September change-log entries now record that v1.95 / v2.52 was published. No claim verdict, scenario weight, precondition state or stakeholder coordinate moves.

entries.title: Twelve defects found by the whole-document review are corrected: source routes, evidence tiers, the signing rule, the fuel chain, water, fiscal arithmetic, the constitutional threshold, listening inferences, actor fields and scenarios
entries.summary: Prepared and held with the v1.95 / v2.52 release, then published with it on 13 September 2026. An independent whole-document review of the held release returned BLOCK on twelve defects (B01–B12), and each is corrected here. Claim sources are now routed explicitly per claim instead of by keyword match, which had sent claims to unrelated articles; 22 cited records already named in the report are registered, and the 12.5% forced-labour tariff now routes to the operative Federal Register notice. Evidence badges distinguish the original record, the news carrier, a stakeholder assertion and an analytical finding; the Senate Committee of the Whole report is refiled from T1-30 to T3-57 as a news carrier. The FAQ, structured data, crawler summary and signing-readiness page now state both branches of the signing rule and all its safeguards, the zero-cost and days-long completion assurances are withdrawn, and 2027 is marked withdrawn as a framework date. The Subic–Clark proposal is a jet-fuel pipeline, not the LNG plant's gas supply; the 1,300 MW figure is a paper shortfall that counts solar nameplate and a study-stage LNG option, not firm committed capacity, and the solar slider tests annual energy and land, not hourly adequacy. Catchment arithmetic no longer asserts that downstream harm is certain; the downstream effect remains undetermined without a basin water balance. The PHP 2.13m implied compensation is stated with its assumptions (a 20% effective rate and 160,000 jobs) and the tax and employment figures are described as not reconciled at current wage benchmarks, not as proof that one must be overstated. Article XVIII, Section 25 exposure is described as contingent on military character, which the civilian record does not show; the stricter recommendation against a bare executive agreement is kept as policy. Negative findings are scoped to what was located, including the conditional US acceptance in principle and the separate MCC grant. Social-listening prose describes sampled, machine-labelled mentions rather than the public, the ×10 population and amplification estimates are withdrawn, and the sentiment exhibit leaves the uncollected 28 July–6 August days blank. Actor commentary is moved out of the gain and cost fields, and blank fields read as unknown rather than no effect. Scenario outcomes are stated as contingent on unmodelled activity mix, utility design and incentive terms, prospective private capital is no longer treated as redeployable to public programmes, and the 10–15-year horizon is flagged as unreconciled with the later ~30-year horizon. Claim verdicts, Key Judgment confidence levels, scenario weights, risk ratings, stakeholder coordinates and precondition states are unchanged; items left for human decision are listed in the private remediation record. This correction does not assert whole-document clearance; before publication each correction was verified against the review's minimum correction, and the corrections that weaken a finding passed the adversarial gate.

entries.title: The 43-officer figure is traced to an initial police report; an inquest bail recommendation, the Palace response, an Angeles City protest and a US official’s remarks are added
entries.summary: Prepared and held with the v1.95 / v2.52 release, then published with it on 13 September 2026. Manila Bulletin reported on 11 September that the Southern Police District initially reported 43 police officers and five activists injured, and SunStar had attributed the same figures to SPD deputy director Col. Robert Baesa on 10 September; Manila Bulletin further reported a later National Capital Region Police Office figure of 16 PNP personnel with minor injuries. No underlying police record was located, so 43 is retained only as an initial SPD figure and is not adopted, and 16 is not an independently verified medical total. Manila Bulletin alone reported that, after inquest, the Taguig City prosecutor’s office issued a certification recommending ₱60,000 bail for each of the five arrested; no certification, court information, posted bail or release was located, and no retrieved record shows a complaint against Teddy Casiño or that any offence occurred. Palace Press Officer Claire Castro’s 11 September remarks in New Delhi and an 11 September protest in Angeles City are added as attributed reports, the latter with no documented attendance count. Ambassador Heather Variava’s remark that the Luzon Economic Corridor is separate from, but connected to, Pax Silica, and her assurance that any agreements would meet both countries’ legal requirements, are added with separate attribution to Context.ph and The Manila Times; no recording or transcript was located, whether the two reports describe one appearance or two is not established, which sense of “Pax Silica” she meant is not established, and the remark is not a legal classification of the proposed New Clark City hub, and the assurance establishes neither the legal form nor the present compliance of any instrument. Adversarial gate: F1–F4 unrefuted with caveats and applied in the gate’s wording; F5 refused as written and applied only in its re-checked replacement. Fifteen sources are registered. A prior high review finding is closed by replacing an unsupported ‘PCO transcript’ description with four freshly retrieved, registered and routed PCO, INQUIRER.net and SunStar sources while retaining the limits on the forum claims. No Key Judgment, confidence level, scenario weight, precondition, red line or claim-checker row moves, and the project-facts date does not move.

entries.title: Cross-surface editorial corrections: source limits, quantitative labels and the signing rule
entries.summary: The full-document review identified inherited contradictions and losses of qualification in the condensed page. The current report and page now carry source-limited police attribution, distinguish a signed separate MCC energy grant from unreviewed legal obligations and zone finance, and register the September sources. The compact footer, workforce deadline, EO 122 evidence pointer, export-period caveats, public-record absence language, Senate/LGU evidence and conditional signing summaries are reconciled with the already-qualified detailed sections. Water downstream effects remain undetermined; solar outputs are annual-energy equivalents, not a firm-capacity design. Activity positions and the two qualitative job-count proxies are explicitly illustrative; chokepoint rows do not share one denominator. CWS and Caritas remain distinct within a mixed church aggregate. Listening counts are unchanged; the plotted window and selected-segment limitations are disclosed, and the unsupported assurance of like-for-like cross-seam comparison is withdrawn. Claim verdicts, KJ confidences, scenario weights, stakeholder coordinates and implementation/precondition states are unchanged. Dated historical logs are retained in the complete append-only changelog JSON and report; the page continues its existing 35-entry display limit, so adding this card moves the oldest displayed entry to the full record. Their older tier/count descriptions are not current evidence classifications. This correction does not assert a new whole-document clearance or fresh verification of every historical source.

entries.title: The previously exhaustive inventory omitted a signed US–Philippine grant instrument
entries.supersedes: The only legally binding instruments in the whole record are Philippine enabling statutes, a separate ACWA Power solar lease, and — on the US side — a tariff against Philippine exports.; The only legally binding instruments in the whole record are Philippine enabling statutes, a separate ACWA Power solar lease, and, on the US side, a tariff against Philippine exports.
entries.summary: That sentence has stood since assessment v2.4, in the report's process-tracing conclusion and on this page. On 10 September 2026 Finance Secretary Frederick Go and US Ambassador Lee Lipton signed the US$60 million Philippines Energy Threshold Program, which the Department of Finance calls a Millennium Challenge Corporation Threshold Program Grant Agreement, with named implementing agencies and an implementation period of four years and nine months. The signed grant instrument must be acknowledged, so the previously exhaustive categorical sentence is withdrawn and rewritten. The adversarial gate refused a mere qualifier twice before the sentence was rewritten. Two things are unchanged. The substantive finding stands: the retrieved record discloses no binding commitment to implement the proposed zone itself, no budget allocation specifically for it, no zone procurement and no project-specific permit. And nothing identifies the grant as a Pax Silica or proposed-zone instrument — it concerns energy-sector governance, and its agreement text was not located in the official repositories searched as at 12 September 2026, so its obligations are not reviewed here. The US tariff is now recorded as an external trade measure rather than an instrument of this project; the gate was asked whether that weakens a finding and held that it corrects a category error. No Key Judgment, confidence level, scenario weight, precondition, red line or claim-checker row moves.

entries.title: The LEC Steering Committee met on 12 May 2026, not 11 May; the zone’s geographic relationship was overstated
entries.supersedes: LEC partnership expanded to eight additional partners; LEC Steering Committee convenes; A separate initiative with its own steering committee. The Zone sits inside its geography; it is not the same instrument
entries.summary: The assessment's timeline has merged two events under 11 May 2026 since v2.41. The trilateral joint statement published by the Philippine Department of Finance is headed “May 12, 2026” and says “Today, our governments convened the LEC Steering Committee”; Japan's embassy in Manila records the fourth LEC Steering Committee as held in Makati on 12 May 2026 and separately says the eight-partner expansion was “announced May 11”. The row is split in two. The error survived because the Philippine Embassy in Washington's own three-page rendering of the same statement carries no date anywhere, and its 15 May posting date is not the statement's date. Separately, the instruments table's claim that the proposed zone “sits inside” the corridor's geography is withdrawn as more definite than the record supports: official descriptions define the corridor by the Subic Bay–Clark–Manila–Batangas connection, not by a surveyed boundary. In its place the government's own words are carried — the Presidential Communications Office's release of 23 July 2026 says “Pax Silica is a proposed high-tech manufacturing and innovation hub under the Luzon Economic Corridor” — with the express limits that this establishes no legally delineated boundary and does not make the corridor, Pax Silica and the proposed-zone instrument legally or institutionally identical.

entries.title: The Luzon Economic Corridor Investment Forum happened, and so did a confrontation outside it
entries.supersedes: The inaugural Luzon Economic Corridor Investment Forum is scheduled for Manila on 10 and 11 September 2026, co-hosted by the governments of the United States, the Philippines and Japan and sponsored by USTDA … Neither USTDA page mentions Pax Silica, semiconductors or New Clark City, so this is a corridor event and not, on its face, a hub event.
entries.summary: The forum opened at the Grand Hyatt Manila in Taguig on 10 September 2026. The page's forward-looking paragraph is replaced by an account of what happened, and the assessment's timeline gains rows for 10 and 11 September. The ellipsis elides an advance attendance figure and a list of planned visits to prospective projects, neither of which is a superseded claim. The second sentence quoted above was an inference drawn from two advance USTDA pages; the event has now superseded it, and a separate adversarial gate cleared its deletion while supplying the narrower finding that replaces it: although Ambassador Lee Lipton linked New Clark City to prospective investment in semiconductors, AI and trusted technologies, no retrieved host-government release identifies the forum itself, or any agreement announced or signed there, as a Pax Silica event or proposed-zone instrument. Outside the forum, a protest directed by its organisers against Pax Silica and the corridor forum became a physical confrontation with police. Later reports placed the arrest count at five, on rosters that do not agree. On the injuries this report declines to adopt the figure most widely printed: several outlets reported 43 injured police officers, but Philstar's own body text gives 16 injured officers from the Southern Police District and 27 injured protesters from rally organisers, which sum to the 43 in its headline, and no retrieved primary police record supports 43 as an officer count. The PNP said its officers exercised maximum tolerance; the organisations present condemned what they called a violent dispersal. On 11 September a Philippine News Agency report available through one republishing outlet quoted the Southern Police District chief as saying police intended to file cases against those arrested, the organisers and Bayan Muna chairperson Teddy Casiño. No primary SPD recording or transcript, independent carrier, complaint, prosecutor’s filing or court record was located; this establishes only the reported announcement, not a filed case or an offence. The same day the Church People-Workers Solidarity, through its chairperson Bishop Gerardo Alminaza of San Carlos, called for a national dialogue and independent environmental, social and human-rights assessments, saying it begins from neither a “predetermined rejection” nor a “blank check”; it is recorded as critical and conditional engagement and is not counted in the opposition coalition.

entries.title: Three status figures on the signing-readiness page become mechanically synchronized
entries.summary: The signing-readiness page published at v1.92 was a wholly dated snapshot. Three of its figures — the 'Status as verified on' date, the preconditions tally in its heading, and the gates count in its heading — now synchronize from the assessment's canonical surfaces (the master's project-facts date row, the live preconditions panel, and the gates checklist data) each time the site publishes, through the same mechanical stamper that synchronizes the site's currency dates. A new surface-consistency invariant refuses publication if any of the three is ever left behind, and the stamper fails closed if the page or its stamp patterns go missing. The page's provenance note is updated to say exactly which figures are mechanical; its narrative remains a dated 10 September 2026 snapshot, unchanged. No assessment content moves.

entries.title: The signing-readiness page joins the navigation
entries.summary: The navigation pills gain a link to /signing-readiness.html, published earlier today at v1.92. The pill navigates to the separate dated page rather than a section of this one, so it carries no scroll-spy active state. No content of the assessment or of the signing-readiness page changes.

entries.title: A dated signing-readiness page is published, and a daily countdown to the November target begins
entries.summary: A new page, /signing-readiness.html, publishes a dated (10 September 2026) monitor-lane report: the countdown to BCDA's qualified November 2026 signing target (counted to both bounds of the target month, since no located source names a day), the verified status of the seven preconditions (0 of 7 met) and the sixteen-gate checklist (2 of 16 closed, both concerning events that predate this assessment's publication), the change-log record between v2.8 and v2.51, and a comparison of the verified record with the §23.3 decision rule. The page is an explicitly dated snapshot: the assessment and its daily-verified panels are canonical and prevail if the two ever differ, and only the day counts on the page update live. The draft was put through the adversarial gate (Codex CLI, gpt-5.6-sol) under refute-default and was refused eight times before clearing on the ninth pass; the published wording is substantially the gate's — among its strikes were every categorical absence claim (rewritten as 'not located as of 10 September 2026'), every prediction, an unearned 'signing window' framing, and a page-authored T-45 milestone now labelled as a page-defined arithmetic marker with no status under the assessment. No finding, Key Judgment, confidence level, scenario weight, precondition or red line moves with this publication.

entries.title: A Pax Silica signatory had already signed the competing framework's establishing agreement, a month before the warning letter was reported
entries.summary: Section 16.1 has carried, since v2.27, Reuters' account of a US State Department draft letter warning signatories they would be excluded from Pax Silica if they joined a competing framework, identified as China's World Artificial Intelligence Cooperation Organization. That passage moved no judgment and still moves none. What moves is the evidentiary record around it, and it now rests on four governments' own publications. Kazakhstan's Ministry of Artificial Intelligence and Digital Development records that on 25 June 2026, in Washington, Deputy Prime Minister and Minister Zhaslan Madiyev signed the Declaration of Accession of the Republic of Kazakhstan to Pax Silica, and that Kazakhstan thereby officially joined. Three weeks later, on 16 July 2026 in Shanghai, Kazakhstan signed the agreement establishing WAICO: a Xinhua report on China's government portal records representatives of 29 countries including Kazakhstan signing it, making their countries WAICO's founding members, and Indonesia's Coordinating Ministry for Economic Affairs published the list of signatory states the same day. Among the 29 states Indonesia names, Kazakhstan is the only one that also appears on the 25-participant Pax Silica roster this assessment uses; Oman signed the WAICO agreement and is not a Pax Silica signatory. Separately, on 9 September 2026 Singapore's Ministry of Digital Development and Information published a parliamentary reply confirming that Singapore, one of the seven original Declaration signatories, has received a WAICO invitation and will consider it, and that there is no ASEAN position on either WAICO or Pax Silica. The proposition advanced is narrow and is the only one advanced: participation in Pax Silica did not prevent Kazakhstan from signing WAICO's establishing agreement before Reuters publicly reported the draft warning. Signature, ratification, entry into force and operative membership are not interchangeable, and we have not seen the WAICO agreement, so Kazakhstan's position there is recorded as signature and a founding-member designation by Chinese official sources, not as accession or established legal membership. The draft letter is undated, so the conduct predates the reporting of it, not demonstrably the draft. Nothing here shows United States knowledge, approval, acquiescence or non-enforcement; nothing corroborates that the draft was authentic, sent, adopted or unchanged; and nothing bears on the Philippines. The finding-level adversarial gate (Codex, gpt-5.6-sol) refused the passage four times before returning UNREFUTED on the fifth. It struck a first draft built on Singapore alone, surfacing Kazakhstan itself as the stronger and earlier case; it refused the word accession for a signature of an establishing agreement; it corrected 'predates the draft letter' to predates Reuters' report of it; it forced the uniqueness claim to be sourced to a full published roster; and it refused an assertion that the reported draft gains nothing at all as an indefensible claim of zero evidential weight. Every caveat is carried. No Key Judgment, confidence level, scenario weight, precondition, red line or claim-checker row moves. The standing signatory count remains 25; a figure of 24 circulating in the day's reporting is not adopted, being the State Department page's own omission of the United States, which section 8.3 already records. Project facts verified to advances to 10 September 2026; comparator, legal and technical dates do not move.

entries.title: The Senate has acted institutionally on procedure; it has not taken a position on Pax Silica's merits
entries.supersedes: the chamber itself has not acted; No committee action or institutional position identified in the sources reviewed
entries.summary: On 8 September 2026 the Senate approved without objection Majority Leader Juan Miguel Zubiri's motion to constitute a Committee of the Whole for extensive discussion of Pax Silica. Senate President Sherwin Gatchalian chairs the committee, with the chairs of Environment, Cultural Communities, Economic Affairs, Trade and Foreign Relations serving as vice chairs. That is an institutional procedural action and it supersedes our statements that the chamber itself had not acted and that no committee action was identified. It is not a substantive disposition. As of 9 September, no source reviewed identified a date for a Committee-of-the-Whole hearing or established that one had already been held; no resulting report, substantive finding, recommendation, approval, rejection, concurrence demand, or institutional Senate position on the project's merits or terms was identified. The adversarial gate returned UNREFUTED_WITH_CAVEATS and required every one of those distinctions. The Senate's influence, stance and dashed encoding are unchanged; the dashed border is now defined expressly as no identified institutional position on the merits, not inactivity. No Key Judgment, scenario weight, claim-checker row or precondition moves.

entries.title: The Philippine Embassy is no longer accurately described as currently passive
entries.supersedes: Holds the treaty channel but is currently passive; High but currently passive
entries.summary: The Philippine Embassy in Washington reported that it attended the 3 September Foundry School launch, and Ambassador Jose Manuel G. Romualdez publicly welcomed the programme as an opportunity for collaboration and workforce preparation. That first-party statement makes our unqualified 'currently passive' description materially misleading, and it is withdrawn. The correction is narrow. Neither the Embassy release nor the State Department fact sheet identifies a Philippine participant or reserved place, Philippine eligibility or selection arrangements, funding or appropriation, an implementing measure, a signed agreement, a Philippine workforce-development plan, or a binding Philippine commitment. The State Department only plans to support participation by Pax Silica economies while working with Congress; it does not promise Philippine participation specifically. The finding-level gate returned UNREFUTED_WITH_CAVEATS and required those limits. No stakeholder magnitude, Key Judgment, scenario weight, claim-checker row or precondition moves.

entries.title: A stale local-government sentence is removed from the site's stakeholder narrative
entries.supersedes: Two sets of actors with decisive power remain conspicuously silent: NGCP and the ERC, who would bear the blame for reserve shortfalls and price effects, and local government, where no independently verified position from the Tarlac provincial government or the municipality of Bamban was located.
entries.summary: The comprehensive post-verification review found that the site's stakeholder narrative still opened with a pre-v2.49 description of local government as absent, then contradicted itself later in the same paragraph by carrying the v2.49 correction. The stale sentence is removed rather than left beside its correction. The current record is retained: Capas has conditionally withheld support pending meaningful consultation, Bamban has sought a public hearing, the province hosted the 19 August consultation, and Governor Yap has welcomed the project; what remains absent is a Sanggunian resolution, published minutes or issues-and-responses register, and a local-government determination on the merits. No magnitude or conclusion moves.

entries.title: We said no project-specific consultation record had been published. The proponent had published one
entries.supersedes: No project-specific consultation record, grievance mechanism, compensation framework, livelihood restoration plan or independent monitoring arrangement has been published.
entries.summary: The Bases Conversion and Development Authority has published a dated account of a project-specific consultation — the 19 August 2026 meeting with the Provincial Government of Tarlac at the Tarlac Convention Center, naming the venue, the participating sectors, the subjects presented and attributed remarks — and, on 4 September 2026, its own account of the Sitio Sapang Kawayan census update with the NCIP. A press release is not minutes, but it is a published record of a consultation, and our categorical wording could not survive it. The first limb of that sentence is withdrawn as overstated. What survives is narrower and still true: no minutes, attendance list, participant submissions, issues-and-responses register, grievance mechanism, compensation framework, livelihood restoration plan or independent monitoring arrangement has been published. The correction runs against us. Our adversarial gate refused the wording we first proposed and supplied the narrower formulation; we have adopted it.

entries.title: We called the Tarlac local government record the largest gap in our evidence base. Three municipalities, the province and the diocese were already on it
entries.supersedes: Capas entered the record procedurally on 31 July 2026 — an information request to BCDA, then a reported meeting BCDA called a step toward consultation — but no LGU has stated a position on the merits, and no independently verified Bamban or provincial position was found: still the largest gap in the evidence base
entries.summary: Three items from mid-August 2026 that we had not carried retire that description. On 11 August Capas Mayor Roseller Rodriguez wrote to President Marcos and to the BCDA invoking Sections 26 and 27 of the Local Government Code, saying the municipality would withhold support until the BCDA held “a meaningful” public consultation — “not supporting, not opposing until there is a public consultation” (BusinessMirror, 13 August). On 17 August Acting Bamban Vice Mayor Levy Tadeo sought a public consultation and named Aeta communities in five sitios of Barangay Anupul — Coop, Gayaman, Malasa, Mabilog and Mainang — as overlapping the project, a second affected-community locus alongside Sitio Sapang Kawayan in Capas; the same report has Tarlac Governor Christian Tell Yap welcoming the jobs and investment (Inquirer, 17 August). On 19 August the BCDA and the provincial government held their consultation. We have rewritten the stakeholder row and raised its influence rating. What is still absent is the formal layer: no Sanggunian resolution, no published minutes or issues-and-responses register, and no local government determination on the merits — Capas has expressly reserved its institutional position until consultation occurs. The sitio-level overlap is a local official’s assertion as reported; it cannot be checked against the parcel while Annex A remains unpublished.

entries.title: Two published accounts of the same consultation, and they do not record the same meeting
entries.summary: The BCDA’s own account of the 19 August 2026 provincial consultation acknowledges generically that questions exist but names no speaker, no objection and no demand. Contemporaneous local reporting the following day records four: the Capas and Concepcion mayors, the acting Bamban vice mayor, and Roberto Calara Mallari, Roman Catholic Bishop of Tarlac, pressing unanswered questions on water, power, displacement and ancestral domain, with the BCDA’s president replying that the hub would bypass community groundwater through rainwater harvesting, river systems and wastewater recycling. We record the divergence as a feature of the published record and draw no inference of concealment from it: a press release is a statement, not minutes. Two things this addition does not establish. It is not a consent process — no account of the meeting identifies an indigenous representative, NCIP participation or any FPIC step, and a proponent-convened dialogue with provincial and municipal officials is not the proceeding IPRA requires. And we do not carry the Concepcion mayor’s quoted “6 Gigawatts”: it doubles the BCDA’s published estimate of about 3 GW, no other source carries it, and our gate could not determine whether it was the mayor’s own figure, a misunderstanding or a transcription error. The 90 million litres per day he cited is consistent with the BCDA’s published 65–90 MLD.

entries.title: We called domestic big business “unaligned”. The Makati Business Club and AmCham had already said otherwise
entries.supersedes: Domestic big business, Ayala, the Makati Business Club, AmCham, is the swing constituency, interested and currently unaligned.
entries.summary: At a Makati Business Club media get-together in Makati on Thursday 3 September 2026, reported on 6–7 September by several outlets apparently covering the same event, MBC chair Edgar O. Chua described Pax Silica and the Luzon Economic Corridor as opportunities for the Philippines while calling for greater transparency, clearer communication and attention to environmental and employment concerns. MBC trustee Cosette Canilao, president and CEO of Aboitiz InfraCapital, was quoted by the Manila Times saying “This is like the next revolution; we cannot [afford not to] be part of it”; we carry that quotation as the Manila Times' rendering, having located no recording, transcript or MBC release containing it. These are reported remarks by a chair and a trustee, not a board resolution or a position paper we were able to locate, and they do not establish Ayala Corporation's position. Our description of domestic big business as “interested and currently unaligned” is therefore withdrawn as to both MBC and AmCham — AmCham having stated on 28 July 2026, in the Joint Foreign Chambers' Arangkada Philippines release, that it welcomed the President's call for support for the Pax Silica Industrial Hub and the Luzon Economic Corridor. We infer no change of position by either organisation: MBC's own commentary on the same address, published 28 July, was already partly favourable, commending the positioning of the initiative while faulting the absence of a concrete roadmap, safeguards and differentiation from PEZA zones. So the date on which MBC adopted its later, more explicit position is not established here, and this is a correction of what we published rather than a record of anyone changing their mind. The adversarial gate refuted our first draft outright and the published wording is substantially the gate's own. It refused the claim that MBC had “moved from interest” to backing as an unestablished claim about timing; refused to let evidence about MBC be read across the aggregated row to Ayala Corp. and AmCham; found our rendering of the Chua quotation unfaithful — the Daily Tribune printed “[B]ottom line, we believe in MBC is that…” and we had silently elided two of its words — so Chua is paraphrased here and not quoted; refused as single-sourced our line that MBC is working with AmCham and the US Embassy to move the initiative forward, which we have not published; and refused to let us restate our own “high if mobilised — currently the swing constituency” characterisation, holding that the remarks demonstrate positions but not pivotal capacity. That phrase is withdrawn from the stakeholder map and not replaced with a new assertion; the standing influence assessment is left unchanged rather than re-argued. The stakeholder exhibit's encoded stance and influence values for this row are unchanged for the same reason. No Key Judgment, confidence level, scenario weight, precondition, red line or claim-checker row moves.

entries.title: House Resolution 1128 was filed on 17 June 2026, not 19 June, and its demand was narrower than we published
entries.supersedes: 19 Jun 2026 | Makabayan bloc files House Resolution 1128 seeking a congressional inquiry into Philippine participation and the Economic Security Zone, demanding disclosure of "all legal instruments, binding commitments, and operational details"
entries.summary: We retrieved the filed text of House Resolution 1128 from the House of Representatives document server and read all four of its pages, and we checked it against the House's own legislative record. Two things we published are wrong. First, the date: we have carried 19 June 2026 as the filing date since our earliest versions. The House measure record gives 17 June 2026, and the filed resolution carries a Bills and Index Service stamp reading "RECEIVED / DATE 17 JUN 2026". We owe readers a further note here: an adversarial gate on an unrelated item, recorded in our own monitoring ledger, had already established the 17 June date, and we never corrected the published figure against it. That was a failure of follow-through, not of retrieval. Second, the scope: we described the resolution as "demanding disclosure of 'all legal instruments, binding commitments, and operational details'". That language sits in a recital. The resolving clause calls for an investigation, in aid of legislation, into Philippine participation in Pax Silica and the establishment of the Economic Security Zone, and nothing further. We now carry the recital as the authors' stated reasons rather than as the resolution's demand. The adversarial gate returned both corrections unrefuted, holding of the second that presenting a recital as the formally resolved demand materially exaggerates the operative text. We also record the resolution's principal authors as the House renders them: Reps. Antonio L. Tinio (ACT TEACHERS), Sarah Jane I. Elago (GABRIELA) and Renee Louise M. Co (Kabataan). It was read on 28 July, referred to the Committee on Economic Affairs, and is pending there since 11 August 2026.

entries.title: There are four House resolutions on Pax Silica, not two — and filing one is not the same as opposing the project
entries.summary: We had named two numbered House instruments, and described House Resolution 1227 as "a second numbered instrument alongside HR 1128". The House of Representatives' own unified search index, checked on 6 September 2026, returns four. Two of them are new to this assessment. House Resolution 1231 was filed on 28 July 2026 by Rep. Alexander Ty Pimentel, whom the filed text's signature block identifies as Chairman of the Special Committee on Strategic Intelligence; it directs that committee to hold a briefing with the Department of National Defense, the National Security Council, the DICT, the DTI, BCDA, the DENR and NGCP, and is pending with the Committee on Rules. House Resolution 1247 was filed on 29 July 2026 by Reps. Edgar R. Erice, Cielo Krisel Lagman, Elijah San Fernando, Presley De Jesus and Leila M. de Lima; it directs eight named committees to inquire into the Pax Silica Agreement and all related undertakings and enumerates eleven questions, the second of which is the legal authority under which the agreement and its implementing arrangements were executed — the question this assessment has asked from the outset. We read the filed texts of all four in full. The adversarial gate refused two of our propositions outright. It refused our claim that filing an inquiry or briefing resolution is not opposition to the project, calling it categorically false: a resolution can be oppositional, supportive, neutral or mixed. The published wording is the gate's own — filing does not by itself establish opposition — and we do not describe the four as opposition instruments or add any of the new authors to the opposition coalition. House Resolution 1231's recitals in fact restate the President's 2026 SONA framing and the administration's investment and jobs projections approvingly. The gate also refused our statement that none of the four has been "calendared, heard or reported out", holding that the measure-status field cannot carry that universal negative and that filing, first reading and referral are themselves legislative actions. What we publish instead is narrower: all four are pending in committee, and no substantive committee disposition, committee report, adopted resolution or institutional House position was located in the House records we searched. That negative is limited by the searches we ran. The four-match search result is likewise bound to the query, the interface, the date and the displayed category, and is not proof that no other instrument exists. No Key Judgment, confidence level, scenario weight, precondition, red line or claim-checker row moves; the gate was asked directly and agreed, noting that the resolutions' recitals of a 130,000-job projection repeat a BCDA figure we already record and add no sixth official employment figure.

entries.title: Two documents leave our not-obtained list: the filed texts of House Resolutions 1128 and 1227
entries.summary: Both were listed among the documents this assessment had not been able to obtain — House Resolution 1128's text since our earliest versions, and House Resolution 1227's since version 2.34, where we recorded that it was not retrievable. Both were retrieved from the House document server on 6 September 2026 and read in full; House Resolution 1128 is an image-only scan, read as rendered pages. They are removed from the not-obtained table and their former unavailability stays visible in the change history, as the adversarial gate required. The gate also required a limit we have applied throughout: a resolution is primary evidence that legislators made the statements in it, and nothing more. House Resolution 1227's recitals assert that the Philippines became the thirteenth member of the Pax Silica Initiative, that the Declaration is non-binding, and that a supplemental agreement was still being finalised. Those are its authors' characterisations. We do not adopt them as independently established facts, and footnoting a government or media release does not turn a recital into a verified project fact.

entries.title: The deadline on DTI-BOI's 128,000-worker target is corrected from 2028 to 2033
entries.supersedes: DTI-BOI's flagship workforce goal is to produce 128,000 engineers and technicians for the semiconductor and electronics industry by 2028
entries.summary: This site and the assessment have carried the Board of Investments' national talent-pipeline target of 128,000 engineers and technicians with a deadline of 2028, in section 12.4, in the section 13.3 jobs comparison, and as a label on the jobs exhibit. The deadline is corrected to 2033. BOI published 2028 in a release of 6 August 2024; its releases of 11 March 2025 and 6 November 2025, and its account of the ITSI semiconductor programme, repeatedly publish 2033, carrying the same figure and the same broad engineer-and-technician formulation. No formal correction, approval or explanation reconciling the two dates has been located or identified, and government material is not fully harmonised — a later TESDA Electronics skills-framework document still carries 2028 — so using 2033 is this report's editorial call on the published record rather than a documented government act, and the published wording says so. The adversarial gate refused two things in the drafting. It struck a claim that the later releases keep “the same worker categories”, because they do not repeat the 2024 release's full spectrum from TESDA-certified technicians through licensed engineers to postgraduates, and because the March 2025 programme is broader in scope than semiconductor and electronics alone. And it struck the inference that a five-year extension strengthens this report's finding that front-end wafer fabrication at New Clark City is unrealistic within any relevant horizon: the 128,000 covers the whole industry rather than the specialised front-end complement, the sources alternate between produce, develop, capacitate and add to the labour pool, no baseline, trajectory, occupational breakdown or New Clark City linkage is published, and nothing establishes that 2033 is slippage rather than changed planning assumptions. What survives is the narrower point the gate itself wrote: workforce availability cannot be assumed on the earlier timetable and may remain a constraint. The fabrication assessment is untouched and rests on its own grounds. The comparison that matters is unaffected in direction — BCDA's low-end job claim for one 1,618.74-hectare parcel would still consume the entire national target.

entries.title: The Philippine semiconductor roadmap is formally launched, and the executive's own bottleneck list is this report's list
entries.summary: On 2 September 2026 the government held a formal launch of the Philippine Semiconductor and Electronics Industry Roadmap for 2026–2030. The launch was not the roadmap's first appearance: it had been presented to the Semiconductor and Electronics Industry Advisory Council in March 2026 and was described by the Board of Investments as moving into implementation during April 2026, and it replaces or updates an earlier semiconductor and electronics roadmap presented through BOI's roadmapping process in 2013 — the roadmap section 12.4 had cited until now. Executive Secretary Ralph Recto, who chairs the Advisory Council, set out 2030 targets: US$110 billion in semiconductor and electronics exports, an increase in the Philippine share of global assembly, test and packaging from 4 to 7 per cent, a 4 per cent share of global electronics manufacturing services, and an integrated-circuit design sector generating US$2 to 3 billion in annual exports. These are recorded as government targets in a launched roadmap — not appropriations, contracts, enrolment places, or evidence that the workforce gap has narrowed. Two things the coverage offered are refused. A circulating figure that semiconductors and electronics are “more than 60 per cent” of Philippine merchandise exports is not adopted: the Philippine Statistics Authority's 2025 figures, which this report carries, give US$45.89 billion and 54.3 per cent. And no statement that the industry is a major driver of Pax Silica is attributed to Recto, because the government news service attributes that description only to the Luzon Economic Corridor. What the launch establishes is narrow and worth recording anyway: the bottlenecks the Executive Secretary named — a shortage of engineers and skilled workers, power, water and logistics infrastructure, slow permitting and regulatory obstacles — are the same list this assessment has compiled against the project from the outside.

entries.title: Foundry School now has a published programme structure, so part of a sentence this report has carried since an early version is withdrawn
entries.supersedes: There is no published workforce development plan, cost, timetable, or training-place target attached to it
entries.summary: Section 12.4 assessed the Stanford Foundry School as a genuine but small and long-dated answer to the Philippine semiconductor workforce problem, and said no workforce development plan, cost, timetable or training-place target was attached to it. The State Department's fact sheet of 3 September 2026, published on the launch, supplies two of those four at programme level: seven regional sessions beginning September 2026 at Arizona State University, Georgia Institute of Technology, The Ohio State University, The Pennsylvania State University, the University of Kansas, Vanderbilt University and Washington University in St. Louis, and a ten-session core programme at Stanford University beginning January 2027 — seventeen sessions in all, each taught by founders and chief executives from advanced manufacturing enterprises. The words “timetable” and “workforce development plan” are therefore withdrawn as to Foundry School itself, and the sentence is rewritten in the Philippine terms it was always about: no cost, no enrolment or training-place allocation, no Philippine participation commitment and no Philippine workforce-development plan is published, and the fact sheet attaches none. The adversarial gate refused an earlier draft of this correction for retaining “no workforce development plan” unqualified when the fact sheet is one. Two things the fact sheet does not establish, and which are not carried as though it did: it names the Republic of Korea, Japan, Taiwan and India as the Pax Silica economies supplying industry leaders and the Philippines is not among them, but the wording is illustrative rather than an eligibility list, so no inference of exclusion is drawn; and its figure of 3.8 million is a projection of United States manufacturing positions needing to be filled by 2033, not a Foundry School output target. No individual session dates and no programme cost are given. The launch itself is recorded at section 8.4 and in the timeline, and it does not change the character of the initiative's four deliverables — a curriculum with a session calendar is still informational, not capital.

entries.title: The proponent agency publishes its own account of the community census — and says the figures are not ready
entries.summary: On 4 September 2026 the Bases Conversion and Development Authority published its own press release, “BCDA, NCIP update community census in Capas, Tarlac for proposed Clark Advanced Manufacturing Park”, describing an updated census of families and residents at Sitio Sapang Kawayan led by NCIP Secretary Nancy A. Catamco and BCDA officer-in-charge senior vice president for the Conversion and Development Group Mark P. Torres. BusinessMirror reported the same day that BCDA clarified to reporters that the exercise is “an update and validation of the existing community census, rather than a new enumeration”, and quoted the agency saying “we are still consolidating and validating the final figures with the NCIP, and we will provide the official numbers once the process is completed”. This is the first occasion located on which the census work appears in the proponent's own published material rather than through NCIP-derived reporting, and what it adds is narrow and first-hand: the agency itself now says no validated count is ready. Section 15.2.1's standing finding — that no current, published, parcel-specific enumeration reporting households and persons on a common reference date has been identified — is re-dated from 23 August to 5 September 2026, and the basis is stated on the page so it can be checked: a fresh negative search made that day of NCIP's own site and nothing wider, where a search for “Pax Silica” returns no result and the News and Events listing shows no item later than 14 August 2026. It is not advanced on BCDA's statement, which cannot establish what was published through some other channel. Whether this is the same field exercise NCIP announced on 20 August, a continuation of it or a related validation is not established, and this report does not decide it. No final official total resulting from the update was located as at 5 September 2026, and the estimates already before the Senate — about 14 houses and “maybe 30”, 75 households, about 1,000 people — are earlier figures that are neither results of this update nor displaced by it. Nothing in BCDA's release identifies the activity as a Section 59 field-based investigation, a Certification Precondition process or an FPIC proceeding, so the process finding stands; no completion date is given; displacement remains disputed; and no Key Judgment, confidence level, scenario weight or precondition moves. The adversarial gate refused this twice before clearing it, once for resting the date advance on BCDA's word alone and once for letting a single-site search carry a claim about publication anywhere.

entries.title: “Clark Advanced Manufacturing Park” is now the proponent's own published name, though still not an adopted one
entries.summary: Version 2.36 admitted the name CAMP only as a reported, hearing-era usage, because its sole support was a reporter's unattributed Filipino sentence about the 14 August 2026 Senate hearing whose pronoun had no stated antecedent. That defect is now cured from the proponent's side. BCDA used “Clark Advanced Manufacturing Park (CAMP)” throughout its own press release of 4 September 2026 and, in a statement to reporters the same day, drew the distinction itself: CAMP is the physical development platform, while Pax Silica is the broader international strategic partnership covering critical minerals, semiconductors, advanced manufacturing and artificial intelligence infrastructure. The name was already attributable to officials at the 14 August hearing, where the Philippine News Agency reported it; what 4 September adds is first-party publication. It does not make CAMP an adopted designation: no proclamation, published board resolution, adopted master plan, procurement instrument or other instrument establishing the name was located, and BCDA's own release calls the park proposed throughout. No BCDA-owned publication using CAMP earlier than 4 September 2026 was located, which is recorded as a search result and not as proof that none exists.

entries.title: The agrarian reform department speaks to the project for the first time, and says no conversion application has reached it
entries.summary: At the House deliberations on the Department of Agrarian Reform's proposed ₱16.935-billion 2027 budget on 3 September 2026, DAR Undersecretary Napoleon Galit answered Gabriela Women's Party-list Representative Sarah Elago that no entity had yet applied for any land-use conversion related to Pax Silica, and said that if lands covered by CLOAs held by agrarian reform beneficiaries were reached by expropriation, DAR would “definitely contest the validity of the exercise of the power of eminent domain by Pax Silica or even the BCDA to that effect”. Both statements are narrower than they read, and section 15.2.2 records them with those limits attached. The absence of a conversion application does not establish that a DAR conversion clearance is required for this parcel: New Clark City sits on BCDA-administered former military reservation land, and whether DAR's conversion jurisdiction attaches depends on the particular parcel's title, classification and whether a valid CLOA covers it, none of which the public record settles. The eminent-domain commitment is expressly conditional, identifies no CLOA-covered land as affected, and describes no expropriation that has been commenced; and Pax Silica is an initiative rather than a juridical person holding expropriation power, so BCDA would be the legally meaningful actor. In putting the question Elago cited BCDA's approximately 4,000 acres or 1,619 hectares and said that, according to the Capas municipal government, over 30 per cent of that area is considered productive agricultural land — that figure is her account of the municipality's position, was not adopted by DAR and was not established at the hearing. What the exchange establishes is the narrow thing: as at 3 September 2026 DAR said at the hearing that it had received no conversion application related to the project. It is recorded because it is the first time the agency with the standing conversion mandate has spoken to this project on the record, and because it corroborates the pre-decisional finding at Key Judgment 16 from a third department. No Key Judgment, confidence level, scenario weight or precondition moves.

entries.title: The preconditions panel's verification date had been frozen at 29 July since the site launched
entries.supersedes: status at 29 july 2026, latest verification: 0 of 7
entries.summary: Exhibit 08's verdict panel carried “status at 29 july 2026” through every revision since launch. The status itself — 0 of 7 preconditions met — was current throughout: the daily editorial run asks the precondition question of every candidate and each day's record states expressly that no precondition moved, most recently on 4 September. Only the displayed date failed to advance, because no stamper or check owned that one line, so the page understated the currency of its own most decision-relevant panel: a reader was told the checklist was last verified five weeks ago when it had been re-verified every morning. The date now reads the project-facts verification date — the daily editorial run is the act that re-verifies the seven — is advanced by the same deterministic stamper that synchronizes the page's other currency stamps and their PDF and crawler echoes, and is enforced as a canonical-date peer by the surface-consistency gate, which fails publication closed if it is ever left behind again. This is the fifth occurrence of the currency-stamp drift class (the prefatory note, corrected at v2.11, v2.18, v2.36 and v2.40) and the first on an exhibit; the class was closed at the source on 2 September for the stamps the stamper knew about — this one it now knows about.

entries.title: A regional competitor named itself one day after this report’s cutoff — Thailand’s “Siam Silica” framework, carried with its qualifications attached
entries.summary: A regional competitor named itself one day after this report’s 26 July 2026 research cutoff, and the report is only now recording it. On 27 July 2026 — the same day as the President’s State of the Nation Address — Thailand’s Ministry of Higher Education, Science, Research and Innovation presented a “Siam Silica” framework at a meeting of the National Higher Education, Science, Research and Innovation Policy Council. §16.3 gains a paragraph and §7 a comparator row. Reporting of the framework describes 2030 targets of eight integrated-circuit design companies, one semiconductor fabrication plant and two advanced packaging facilities, with an associated workforce requirement of just under 3,000 specialists. Two qualifications travel with those figures wherever they appear in this report: the framework was presented and referred for an implementation plan — not adopted, approved or funded — and the Thai policy office’s own English account states the numbers conditionally, as the premise of a workforce-sizing exercise rather than as commitments. The report applies to Bangkok the standard it applies to Manila. The item reached this report through a source the same day’s news lane rejected: a Rappler opinion column of 3 September 2026, refused for the news rail as opinion, whose unattributed comparator passage was not taken on its own authority but checked independently against the Thai policy office’s own record and three independent outlets. One adversarial gate pass (Codex gpt-5.6-sol) over six numbered claims: none refuted, five returned with caveats, every caveat honoured. The gate corrected the drafter’s institutional construction — NXPO is the Office of the Council, not the Council — required “framework” over “programme”, and forbade “adopted”, “approved”, “funded” and “is deploying”. It also refused, on the record, every figure the column itself offered, and none of the four is carried anywhere in this report: the “200-billion-baht subsidy pool” (unsubstantiated; the likely origin is Thai BOI reporting of more than ฿200 billion in private printed-circuit-board investment applications across 180 projects), the “unified, single-board regulatory framework” (coordination was proposed, not established), the “US$5.3 billion [Penang] state fund” (Malaysia’s RM25 billion was federal support for its national semiconductor strategy, announced May 2024), and Vietnam’s “37-year preferential tax rates” (a 5% rate for qualifying large projects, not a generic one). No Key Judgment, confidence level, scenario weight, precondition, red line or claim-checker row moves; the gate was asked directly and answered no, and separately confirmed that Key Judgment 1’s description of Thailand’s established automotive specialisation should be left alone, a newly presented framework being a different thing from an established industrial position. “Project facts verified to” does not advance and stays at 3 September 2026: this is a regional comparator, not a fact about the project, and the day’s sweep surfaced no new project development. The site’s own section text is unchanged — it does not carry §16.3 — so this release moves the version markers and this log, and the change itself lives in the assessment master and its PDF.

entries.title: A second government’s foreign ministry says the Declaration would create no legal obligations — and a twenty-sixth signatory is one step away without the count moving
entries.summary: On 2 September 2026 the Lithuanian government approved the country’s participation in the Pax Silica Declaration and in a separate US-proposed critical-minerals agreement. Lithuania’s Ministry of Foreign Affairs said in doing so that neither instrument is an international treaty and that neither would create legal obligations for Lithuania under international or national law — in the Lithuanian original, that they „nėra tarptautinės sutartys“ and „Lietuvai nesukurtų teisinių įsipareigojimų“. §8.2 carries that as corroboration of this assessment’s existing reading and expressly not as its foundation: the non-binding conclusion has always rested on the Declaration’s own operative language, and a foreign ministry’s characterisation of an instrument to its own cabinet is interested evidence, since it is also what allows an executive to join without parliamentary ratification. §8.3 records the accession step as an approval to join and not an accession. The Cabinet’s published meeting record establishes only that the matter was before it as agenda item 2; LRT/BNS establishes the outcome; the meeting protocol and the ministry’s submission were not retrievable, and neither an executed instrument, nor a Lithuanian signature announcement, nor a State Department media note welcoming Lithuania was located as at 3 September 2026. The standing signatory count therefore remains 25, and Lithuania remains among the eleven economies that signed the separate Joint Statement on AI Opportunity without acceding to the Declaration. Four adversarial gate passes ran (Codex CLI, gpt-5.6-sol); the first three each refused something. The first refused the claim that the Cabinet agenda record documented the decision, on the ground that an agenda establishes consideration and not the outcome, and struck an implication that Lithuanian accession is inevitable. The second refused the chronology row for converting the Lithuanian conditional into a categorical present tense; the original was then checked directly and the gate was right. The third required three further repairs, each turning a not-located search result back into a not-located result rather than proof of absence. The fourth found no defect. No Key Judgment, confidence level, scenario weight, precondition, red line or claim-checker row moves — the gate was asked at every pass and agreed each time, adding that strengthening confidence on a single interested government’s characterisation would be disproportionate.

entries.title: A cabinet department says its own assessment is unfinished; the Palace answers the “another location” question
entries.summary: Two official statements of 1 September 2026, recorded from a sweep of 88 candidates of which the adversarial gate let one onto the news rail. At the House budget briefing on the Department of Agriculture’s 2027 budget, Gabriela Women’s Party Rep. Sarah Elago asked whether the department had assessed the project’s effects, citing reports that around 15,000 farmers and up to 20,000 Aeta people could lose their livelihoods and ancestral lands. Agriculture Secretary Francisco P. Tiu Laurel Jr. answered that the department is “still thoroughly assessing the full effects of Pax Silica” and that “our assessment is not yet finished”, estimating “perhaps, in another 30 days”, while offering an expressly tentative impression that “not that many people will be affected” — based partly, he said, on what he had seen on television. No DA administrative order, terms of reference, scope, method, team or commitment to publish was located here, so the thirty days is an estimate given under questioning and not a documented departmental timetable. Section 15.2.2 records this as preserving the finding that the affected-household count is unknown while adding mixed evidence: the unfinished assessment reinforces the uncertainty, and the Secretary’s impression points toward the lower end of the dispute without verifying any figure. That balance is the gate’s doing. Its most important catch was that our first draft presented the item as pure reinforcement of our own finding and suppressed the direction of the Secretary’s impression; the published wording is its correction. Separately, at a Malacañang press briefing, Palace Press Officer Claire Castro, attributing the position to the DTI, said “On the Clark Advanced Manufacturing Park, there will be no data centers” and that, as to any other site, “there is no proposal yet regarding this”. Section 5.1 records it as the most categorical official assurance yet and leaves the finding unweakened, because an assurance is not an instrument: no proclamation, board resolution, master plan or bid document defining the Park was located, and the statement sets no data-centre threshold, no own-use boundary, no decision-maker and no change-control rule. The gate refused three of the four rail items. It killed both Palace headlines — BusinessWorld’s for moving Castro’s boundary from New Clark City to “Clark”, which are not the same place, and BusinessMirror’s for adding “formal” to “no proposal yet” while its lede read that as no company having formally applied — and when asked which of the two it would allow onto an evidence-sensitive rail it answered “neither”. Because the rail carries publishers’ headlines verbatim, neither is on it; the substance is written here in our own words instead. It also killed the State Department’s own notice of the Foundry School launch, on the prospective-versus-completed distinction: the headline says “Launches”, the body says the launch will occur on 3 September, and the notice establishes no Philippine role and no new money. Six gate passes ran in all; both finding texts were refused three times before clearing. Among the other catches: the claim that the DA holds “the clearest mandate” over the affected livelihoods, struck because the Aeta ancestral-land dimension sits with the NCIP; “ten weeks before” the November signing, struck twice as false precision; two truncated quotations and one splice; and a draft assertion that Castro’s statement was “not a statement about the parcel’s permitted uses”, struck as false once the gate established that official reporting uses the Park’s name for the proposed development itself. No Key Judgment, confidence level, scenario weight, precondition, red line or claim-checker row moves. The date to which project facts are verified advances to 2 September 2026.

entries.title: The water supply enters procurement — a bidder, a price and a December target, and still no water balance
entries.summary: On 28 August 2026 the BCDA Board granted original proponent status to a consortium of Maynilad Water Services Inc. and the Korea Water Resources Corporation (K-water), the operator of Angat Dam, for an unsolicited proposal reported at ₱14.8 billion to supply water and manage wastewater at New Clark City. It must still clear the public–private partnership process and a Swiss challenge, and BCDA’s December 2026 award date is a conditional target. This is the first concrete procurement step toward the water this report calls the binding constraint, and the first thing to say about it is what it is not: original proponent status is not a contract award, not a construction commitment, and not evidence that the water exists. Three BCDA figures arrived with it, all attributed and none verified. New Clark City’s existing capacity is an estimated 20–30 million litres a day. Estate capacity could rise to as much as 150 MLD, with the initial system designed for up to 135 MLD. And contemporaneous reporting of the grant repeated BCDA’s earlier estimate that Pax Silica could eventually require 65–90 MLD. Two ratios follow: this one project wants between 2.2 and 4.5 times everything New Clark City can supply today, and roughly half to two-thirds of the initial designed capacity of a system that must also serve every other user in the estate. Those are offered as scale and not as an allocation — nothing establishes that the 135 MLD would be available here, and the system is an estate-wide utility rather than a Pax Silica project. What the procurement step does not supply is the thing the water section has asked for throughout. As at 1 September 2026 no water balance, catchment delineation, dry-season yield analysis, flow-duration curve, dependable drought yield, withdrawal inventory or environmental-flow reservation for this system was located in publicly available BCDA, Maynilad, K-water, NWRB or DENR-EMB material, and the announcement of the grant identifies no selected catchment. We state that as a publication finding rather than a claim that no such work exists — an unsolicited proposal accepted to this stage presumably rests on technical work, and the point is that none of it is public at the moment the process moves. A December award on a proposal whose water balance has never been published would place the contract ahead of the evidence. The catchment arithmetic does not change and neither does the conclusion it supports. Separately, the social-screening section records the launch in Quezon City on 31 August 2026 of the Network Opposed to Pax Silica, the first named national multi-sectoral coalition against the project, at which Petronila Capiz-Muñoz, identified as chieftain of the Aeta community at Sitio Sapang Kawayan, said the community had not been consulted and had again been told to leave, this time by December. That is attributed testimony; its weight is that it carries in the chieftain’s own voice, at a public event, the account this report has held since 18 August from two other residents. It establishes no official deadline, and displacement remains disputed. The adversarial gate ran one pass over five numbered claims and refuted one of them: the drafter had written that BCDA restated the 65–90 MLD requirement, and the gate held that the BCDA-derived announcement does not itself restate it, so the published wording is the gate’s own. It also struck a categorical claim that no hydrological analysis exists in favour of the dated publication finding above, forbade any implication that the 135 MLD would be available to this project, forbade describing the system as rainwater-only, forbade adopting a concession term while February reporting says 50 years and Maynilad’s August disclosure says 25, and required the chieftain’s account to be carried strictly as testimony. Asked directly whether any of this justifies moving a key judgment, confidence level, scenario weight, precondition or red line, it answered no. Nothing moves. One figure was adjudicated at rail level and is recorded here because the record should show it: the Manila Bulletin reported the project as ₱5 billion in its headline and ₱4.8 billion in its body, against ₱14.8 billion in BusinessMirror, the Philippine News Agency and the roughly ₱15 billion reported when the proposal first surfaced in February. The gate held ₱14.8 billion safe to carry; only that figure is used.

entries.title: One dated thing now sits between today and November — a corridor investment forum, and it is not a Pax Silica event
entries.summary: The timeline gains 10–11 September 2026: the inaugural Luzon Economic Corridor Investment Forum in Manila, co-hosted by the governments of the United States, the Philippines and Japan and sponsored by the US Trade and Development Agency, convening a stated 600 investors, industry leaders and senior officials. USTDA's own .gov pages establish every element of that — the dates, the venue, the three co-hosts, the 600 figure, programme themes including advanced manufacturing, a partner list running from Australia to the United Kingdom, visits to prospective project locations at Subic Bay, Clark and Batangas, and attendance that is 'restricted and subject to approval'. What those pages do not do is mention Pax Silica, semiconductors, New Clark City or the proposed economic security zone, and the new row says so on its face. The forum is recorded because it dates the window before the November framework target, not because it evidences anything about the hub. The item reached this report sideways. A Bulatlat report published 28 August carried the argument of ILPS Philippines' secretary-general that Executive Order No. 122 was issued ahead of this forum; the adversarial gate, checking that report, confirmed the forum independently against USTDA and supplied the exact dates.
